fixes.explanation: Offerings do show up in this chapter, friend. In verse 29, Moses offers the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. But the lifting cloud means something else. When it lifts from above the tabernacle, the Israelites set out on their journey. Offerings stay at the altar, and the people move when the cloud moves.

Nothing here says Aaron will sit and settle people's disputes, friend. This is about a different job. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and anoint him and consecrate him “…so that he may serve Me as a priest.” Priest is the role, and this passage doesn't hand him a judge's seat.

A cloud, baker! Moses finishes the work in verse 33, and then the cloud covers the Tent of Meeting. The verse says “…the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” Verse 35 adds that Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it. Bases, frames and crossbars all set up, and then this happens.

Gathering to hear Moses is a fair guess, friend, but in these verses the cloud is the signal. When it lifts, the Israelites set out. Verse 37 adds that if it was not lifted, they would not set out until the day it was taken up. And verse 38 says the cloud was in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.
